context.guidance: Serve every route that carries Personal Data over TLS only, and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes on session cookies. Replace wildcard cross-origin rules with an explicit list of trusted origins. These transport and session controls are part of the safeguards Rule 6(1)(a) requires for the Personal Data they carry.

value.fix: Stop serving Juice Shop traffic over plain HTTP. Change the port-80 `aws_lb_listener.http` so it no longer forwards requests to the target group. Its default_action should be a permanent redirect to HTTPS: `default_action { type = "redirect" redirect { port = "443" protocol = "HTTPS" status_code = "HTTP_301" } }`. Then add a TLS listener: `resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" { load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.juice_shop.arn port = 443 protocol = "HTTPS" ssl_policy =«SECRET» certificate_arn = aws_acm_certificate_validation.juice_shop.certificate_arn default_action { type = "forward" target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.juice_shop.arn } }`. This needs a validated ACM certificate for the app's domain, and the ALB security group must allow inbound 443. Set the ALB's `drop_invalid_header_fields = true`. To complete the SEC-11 controls in the application, send `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`, set session and auth cookies with `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict` (or `Lax`), and replace any wildcard CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with an explicit list of trusted origins. After the change, `curl -I http://<alb-dns>` should return a 301 to https://, and the HTTPS endpoint should accept only TLS 1.2 and above.
